Did we not go see them last year?

Hey, let's just go grab a drink.
Let's go to karaoke and I will sing Cherry Blossom Ending for you.

I was busy today because of cherry blossoms.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

meanings.note: Basic verb of motion. With the respectful ending -세요 in 안녕히 가세요, it forms the polite farewell 'Goodbye!'. RR: gada.

examples.trans: I am going home.
Go safely!
Did you hear about this tomorrow?
I was busy today because of tomorrow.

meanings.note: Used with 오다 or 내리다.

examples.trans: It is raining.
The rain stopped.

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)
meanings.note: Used in expressions like 혼란이 오다 (confusion comes) or 비가 오다 (rain falls)

examples.text: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.
examples.trans: It's been one year since I came to Korea.
I suddenly started feeling sleepy.
Did you hear about this flowers?
I was busy today because of flowers.

meanings.note: Placed before the verb it modifies.

examples.trans: I finished all my homework.
I ate all the rice.
I want to fall off, you know right now.
How about trying to fall off, you know together tomorrow?
Come on, nice to meet you!
Come on, I understand now.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.
Let's must edit together today.
I worked hard to must edit yesterday too.
Did you hear about this next year?
I was busy today because of next year.

meanings.note: expresses surprise, exasperation, or sympathy

examples.trans: Goodness, it's already this late!
Oh dear, how hard was it?
I understand well (every year).
Today is a (every year) busy day.
I want to blooming right now.
How about trying to blooming together tomorrow?
Did you hear about this this year?
I was busy today because of this year.
I understand well (unusually).
Today is a (unusually) busy day.

meanings.note: colloquially often pronounced/written 이쁘다

examples.trans: The flowers are really pretty.
This color is prettier.

meanings.note: 1st person plural pronoun; also used for 'my' with family, school, or workplace

examples.trans: Our team has a good atmosphere.
Let's eat lunch together tomorrow.
Did you hear about this last year?
I was busy today because of last year.

않다.gloss: to not do, to not be

meanings.en: to not do, to not be
meanings.note: Auxiliary negative verb/adjective used after -지 (long-form negation)

examples.trans: The weather isn't cold today.
I didn't say anything.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb.

examples.trans: Why are you running?
Why were you late today?

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Used in -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같다 to express 'it seems that...' or 'I think...'.

meanings.en: to be the same, to be like
meanings.note: Compares two things with -와/과 같다.

examples.trans: I think I'm late.
It looks like it's going to rain.

meanings.note: Casual exclamation used to call someone younger or a close friend.

examples.trans: Hey, come quickly!
Hey, where are you going?
Did you hear about this drinks or something?
I was busy today because of drinks or something.
I want to drink right now.
How about trying to drink together tomorrow?
Did you hear about this karaoke room?
I was busy today because of karaoke room.
Did you hear about this ending?
I was busy today because of ending.

meanings.note: 르-irregular verb; conjugates as 불러요 in polite present, but 부르면 in conditional.
Used with 노래 ('song'): 노래를 부르다.

examples.trans: The team leader called you to the conference room.
Please call my name loudly.

meanings.note: Used for giving things to someone of equal or lower status.

examples.trans: I gave a gift.
Please give me some water.

meanings.note: Used when repeating an action.

examples.trans: See you again!
It is raining again.

meanings.note: Action of coming together with someone.

examples.trans: I meet a friend.
Let's meet tomorrow.
